metadata.title: Erick All - Hits IR, ACL tear feared
metadata.description: The Bengals placed All (knee) on injured reserve Tuesday.
metadata.analysis: Though All will be eligible to return from IR as soon as Week 12, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network relays that the third-year tight end is feared to have sustained a season-ending ACL tear of his right knee during Sunday's 35-13 win over the Ravens. All will likely undergo further testing over the next day or two before the Bengals provide an updated diagnosis, but if the ACL tear is confirmed, the 26-year-old could be sidelined into the 2027 season. He previously tore the ACL in the same knee in 2023 during his final collegiate season at Iowa and during his 2024 rookie campaign with Cincinnati.

metadata.title: Bengals Place Erick All Jr. on Injured Reserve With Torn ACL
metadata.description: The Cincinnati Bengals placed tight end Erick All Jr. (knee) on Injured Reserve on Tuesday with what is believed to be a torn ACL that he suffered in the Week 7 win over the division-rival Baltimore Ravens on Sunday, a source told Ian Rapoport of the NFL Network. In a corresponding move, the Bengals signed tight end Cam Grandy off the Minnesota Vikings' practice squad. All, the team's fourth-round pick in 2024 from Iowa, finished Sunday's win by catching all three of his targets for 36 yards before injuring his knee. It is devastating news for the 26-year-old, who already tore the same ACL during his rookie campaign with the Bengals. He caught eight of his nine targets through six games this year for 56 yards and no touchdowns after he had a 20-158-0 line in nine games in his rookie season in 2024. All missed the entire 2025 campaign and now faces another long recovery before trying to get ready for the start of the 2027 season next fall. His season-ending knee injury opens up more playing time for Drew Sample the rest of the way behind starting TE Mike Gesicki, who has caught a touchdown pass in four straight games.

metadata.title: Erick All - Won't return Sunday with knee injury
metadata.description: All (knee) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's game against the Ravens.
metadata.analysis: All appeared to suffer the injury while making a catch in the third quarter. He'll be sidelined for the rest of Sunday's game, so Drew Sample and Jack Endries are both in line for more snaps the rest of the way.

metadata.title: Erick All Jr. catches three passes Sunday
metadata.description: Erick All Jr. caught three passes for 25 yards in Sunday's 31-24 win over the Cincinnati Bengals.
metadata.analysis: All was technically Cincinnati's second leading receiver on Sunday, despite racking up just 25 yards over the course of the afternoon. He has showcases potential but isn't expected to be a relevant fantasy option moving forward.

metadata.title: Erick All - Catches two passes in win
metadata.description: All notched two receptions (on three targets) for five yards during Sunday's 20-6 win versus the Texans.
metadata.analysis: All logged 25 offensive snaps in Week 2, ending behind Drew Sample (36) and Mike Gesicki (21). After not seeing any attention from Joe Burrow in the 33-27 win over the Buccaneers in Week 1, the 26-year-old was targeted three times versus the Texans, catching two passes for five yards. All finished his rookie campaign with 20 receptions for 158 yards. He didn't play in 2025 due to a knee injury. While All should be on the field from week-to-week, assuming he stays healthy, he likely won't do anything meaningful for fantasy managers, especially with Gesicki, Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins and Chase Brown in the equation.

metadata.title: Erick All Jr. Not a Featured Piece in Crowded Bengals Passing Game
metadata.description: A fourth-round pick in the 2024 NFL Draft, Cincinnati Bengals tight end Erick All Jr. flashed some upside as a rookie before missing the entire 2025 season due to a torn ACL. All Jr. is back healthy for the start of the 2026 season. However, the 26-year-old was not involved in the Cincinnati passing game in Week 1, going without a target or a reception in the Bengals' 33-27 victory over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. All Jr. was one of four tight ends used by the Bengals, and it was veteran tight end Mike Gesicki who dominated the receiving work with five catches for 78 yards and a touchdown on seven targets. While All Jr. could eventually work his way into more opportunities, it will likely be difficult for him to establish a fantasy-relevant role barring multiple injuries in the Cincinnati tight end room.

metadata.title: Erick All - Plays on 20 snaps
metadata.description: All saw 20 offensive snaps but didn't get a target during Sunday's 33-27 win over the Buccaneers.
metadata.analysis: The 2024 fourth-round pick operated as the third tight end behind Drew Sample (41 snaps) and Mike Gesicki (21 snaps). All made 20 catches as a rookie two years ago before missing the 2025 campaign with a right-knee injury. He doesn't seem like much of a factor in the receiving game right now.

metadata.title: Erick All - Cleared for camp
metadata.description: All (knee) passed his conditioning test and is all set to participate in training camp, Dan Hoard of the Bengals' official site reports.
metadata.analysis: All underwent multiple knee surgeries for an ACL injury that sidelined him for the entire 2025 season. The 2024 fourth-rounder will be competing with Tanner Hudson and Drew Sample to serve as the No. 2 tight end behind Mike Gesicki.

metadata.title: Erick All - Getting eased back into action
metadata.description: All (knee) has been cleared to participate at training camp in a limited capacity, Chris Roling of USA Today reports.
metadata.analysis: It's an encouraging update for All, who was sidelined for the entire 2025 campaign after complications from a surgery to repair a ruptured ACL he suffered in November of 2024. He'll be competing with veteran Tanner Hudson and rookie seventh-rounder Jack Endries for positioning on the bottom half of the tight end depth chart in 2026.

metadata.title: Erick All - Participating in OTAs
metadata.description: All (knee) participated in Cincinnati's offseason training activities Tuesday, Paul Dehner of The Athletic reports.
metadata.analysis: All is making progress in his recovery from a torn ACL that held him out of the entirety of last season. The 25-year-old last appeared in a regular-season game in 2024 but will look to make his return during the upcoming campaign.

metadata.title: Erick All - Placed on reserve/PUP list
metadata.description: The Bengals placed All (knee) on the reserve/PUP list Tuesday.
metadata.analysis: The move technically means that All would be eligible to return after missing a minimum of four regular-season games. However, the 2024 fourth-rounder is not expected to play in 2025 while recovering from a torn ACL in his right knee that he suffered in Week 9 of his rookie season. He's suffered the same injury to his right knee twice in the last two seasons dating back to his final year at Iowa, so the Bengals will take All's rehab cautiously, with the hope that he will be fully healthy for 2026.

metadata.title: Erick All - Unlikely to play until 2026
metadata.description: All (knee) is expected to miss the entire 2025 season, James Rapien of SI.com reports.
metadata.analysis: All is present for training camp, but merely as an observer with a large brace around his right knee. He tore the ACL in his right knee both of the past two seasons, limiting him to seven games in his final collegiate campaign and nine appearances as an NFL rookie. The 2024 fourth-round pick apparently will take his rehab slower this time, focusing on 2026 and beyond rather than trying to make it back at some point this season.

metadata.title: Erick All Jr. (knee) placed on PUP list
metadata.description: The Bengals placed TE Erick All Jr. on the PUP list.
metadata.analysis: All is considered likely to miss the whole season after tearing his ACL for the second time in his career.

metadata.title: Erick All - Moved to PUP list
metadata.description: The Bengals placed All (knee) on the active/PUP list Saturday, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.
metadata.analysis: All tore the ACL in his right knee in Week 9 last season and spent the remainder of the campaign on IR. While the 24-year-old is technically eligible to return to practice at any point as long as he's medically cleared, there's a strong chance that he'll need to sit out the entire 2025 season while rehabbing from the injury.
